melder.utilities.general_base.cleanable.label: cleanable
melder.utilities.general_base.cleanable.role: The single teardown contract shared across the entire runtime.
responsibilities: define explicit cleanup, idempotent for calls that do not overlap
provide check_cleaned so post-teardown use fails loudly

melder.utilities.general_base.cleanable..label: Cleanable
responsibilities: defines cleanup that is idempotent for calls that do not overlap, and the cleaned-state guard expectations
provides using_cleanup() and async_using_cleanup() helper contexts that clean up at most once and let cleanup errors propagate

sets the lock policy for subclasses: one deletes its lock last by default, so a second cleanup already waiting on it returns but one that loads it after the deletion raises AttributeError (cleaning one object from two threads is the caller's mistake); one whose cleanup a Melder path can overlap keeps its lock and documents it (Spell, Creations, FrameLinkContract), and a kept lock references nothing, so it never keeps the object alive (2026-11-08, GitHub #271)

melder.utilities.general_base.cleanable..label: _CleanupContext
melder.utilities.general_base.cleanable..role: Internal context helper supporting the Cleanable teardown contract.
responsibilities: drops its owner reference, calls cleanup() at most once and lets its error propagate without suppressing the block's exception

melder.utilities.general_base.cleanable..label: _AsyncCleanupContext
melder.utilities.general_base.cleanable..role: Async counterpart of the cleanup context, driving async_cleanup().
responsibilities: drops its owner reference, awaits async_cleanup() at most once and lets its error propagate without suppressing the block's exception

edges_authored.why: Cleanable is the concrete lifecycle base whose public surface is mirrored by ICleanable.
